written: 2026-10-07. Committed, with src/run.mjs and src/score.mjs, before any full run. Development used one smoke-test agent search (gpt-5-mini, B = 20, market seed 500, a seed outside the registered ranges) and compute-only checks of the generator, grammar and baselines on seeds 1-240.
author: Arhan Canli
question: When an LLM agent searches trading strategies with a backtest tool and adapts each trial to earlier results, is the deflated Sharpe ratio (DSR) still calibrated, and what does protect against false discoveries?
closest_prior_work: Gençay (2026, arXiv:2608.27734) deflates an LLM agent's best strategy by its recorded trial count on real data, without ground truth and without testing calibration under adaptivity.

markets.shape: 100 assets, 10 characteristics (AR(1), phi 0.99, standardized daily), 756 design days and 504 held-out days; market factor 1% and idiosyncratic 2% daily volatility; trading cost 5 bp per unit traded.
markets.alternative: Seeds 2000001-2000100: characteristic (seed mod 10) at a one-day lag, target annualized Sharpe 2.0 for its quintile spread (realized about 82% of target in development).
markets.baseline_only: Seeds 3000001-3002000 (null) and 4000001-4001000 (alternative, same rule): random and grid search only, for precise baseline rates.

searchers.agent: Adaptive: backtests up to 10 strategies per call, sees every result, then submits one strategy and an expected Sharpe ratio; at most 40 turns.
searchers.agent_na: Non-adaptive: proposes its strategies in one call before seeing any result; the best by design-window Sharpe is reported.
searchers.random: B distinct strategies uniformly at random (seed = market seed).
searchers.grid: Coarse-to-fine grid: every characteristic at each setting before the next, first B.

model_settings: OpenAI chat completions, provider-default temperature, tool_choice required; prompts are fixed in src/searchers.mjs.

outcomes.certified_counted: DSR >= 0.95 with N = recorded trials and the ledger's cross-trial Sharpe dispersion.
outcomes.certified_effective: DSR >= 0.95 with N = round(participation ratio of the trials' return correlations), at least 2.
outcomes.holdout_reject: One-sided t-test at 5% that the reported strategy's mean held-out daily return is above zero.
outcomes.found_planted: Under the alternative, the reported strategy uses the planted characteristic with sign +1.
outcomes.overclaim: Agent's stated expected Sharpe minus the reported strategy's held-out Sharpe (adaptive agent only).
outcomes.n_eff_ratio: Effective trials divided by recorded trials.

predictions.statement: Null, B = 100, both models pooled: the adaptive agent is certified (certified_counted) more often than random search on the same markets; one-sided exact McNemar test on discordant pairs, alpha 0.05.
Null: holdout_reject has a rate of at most 7% for every searcher, budget and model (an untouched held-out window keeps the test near its level whatever the search).
Null, B = 100, both models pooled: the adaptive agent's n_eff_ratio is below random search's on the same markets in more than half of the markets; one-sided sign test, alpha 0.05.
Null, both budgets and models pooled: the adaptive agent's mean overclaim is above zero; one-sided t-test, alpha 0.05.
Alternative, B = 100, both models pooled: the adaptive agent reports the planted strategy more often than random search on the same markets; one-sided exact McNemar test, alpha 0.05.

failures: A search that errors (API failure, no submission) is retried once on the same market; if it fails again it is reported as failed and excluded from rates, with the count reported.
reporting: Every cell is reported whether or not a prediction holds. src/score.mjs scores the predictions without hand input. Nothing in this file is changed after the runs start; anything else is exploratory.
